SMTO-CFG-0068 — SMTO's Fast Cache was set up with an unsupported size

GUID: 71998b37-2ebc-402b-bef2-fde5698595b2
Slug: cache-bound-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO tried to prepare Fast Cache, which keeps exact prompts and their checked read steps, with a size it doesn't support. There is no setting in the app for this size.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If someone changed SMTO's program files or added a custom add-on that sets the Fast Cache size, ask them to undo that change or use a number from 1 to 256. Standard SMTO always uses 256 entries, so only a change to its code can produce another size.
  2. Update SMTO from Settings › Setup › Server updates, or run the installer again, then start SMTO. A clean installation puts back the standard Fast Cache size.
  3. Then repeat what you were doing. If it was a task, first open its conversation and check whether it already ran. Part of the work may have finished before SMTO stopped, so checking avoids doing it twice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts normally and Settings › Agent behavior › Fast Cache opens without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and mention any custom changes made to the installation. Don't change timeouts, budgets or other limits to get around this; they don't control the cache size.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • VerifiedExecutionCache or MemoryExecutionCache was constructed with max_entries outside the supported range of 1 to 256.

What this means

  • Verified execution cache construction finds max_entries outside the accepted 1–256 range. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Verified execution cache construction finds max_entries outside the accepted 1–256 range.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the cache entry-count configuration rather than model context or byte-output limits.

How to fix it

  • Find the caller passing max_entries; stock callers (execution_cache/runtime.py, execution_cache/management.py, runtime_state/bootstrap.py) all use the default 256. Pass an integer from 1 to 256, or reinstall to restore the stock modules if no local change is intended. This bound is cache capacity only, not model context or shell output.
  • Set the cache bound within the documented range. This controls cache capacity, not model context or shell output.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended cache count validates within its supported bound.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
